NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard practice delivers a procedural/parameter intervention (CIP schedule and chemistry adjustment) to mitigate scale-driven thermal stress and CIP inefficiency. The draft’s departure is an increase in caustic concentration to address organic soils, which ignores the inorganic scale driver. The correct mechanism departure is reducing the time-averaged inorganic scale mass per duty cycle to maintain thermal uniformity and preserve caustic efficacy, utilizing the permitted axis of CIP concentration and schedule.

PHYSICS CHECK
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = time-averaged inorganic scale mass on plates; the mechanism moves it DOWN by increasing acid descaling frequency (fortnightly) and maintaining moderate caustic strength to prevent organic interference; this REDUCES the differential thermal conductivity between plated and un-plated areas, lowering the thermal stress integral that drives blistering.
MECHANISM CLASS: Chemistry and Schedule Optimization (CIP Parameter Tuning).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
1. CIP Schedule Modification: Change acid descal interval from standard (e.g., monthly) to fortnightly. Tag: USER CONSTRAINT (Draft says "acid descal fortnightly"). Rationale: Reduces scale thickness accumulation time, keeping plates clean for heat transfer. (c)
2. CIP Caustic Setpoint Verification: Maintain caustic at 0.8 mol/L (approx. 3.2 wt% NaOH) at 70 C. Tag: CALCULATED (0.8 mol/L NaOH * 40 g/mol = 32 g/L = 3.2 wt% assuming density ~1.0). Rationale: The draft's concentration exceeds the gasket rating. (c)
3. Gasket Replacement/Verification: Verify gasket material compatibility with 3.2 wt% NaOH at 70 C against the 2.5 wt% limit. Tag: USER CONSTRAINT (Gaskets rated for up to 2.5 wt% NaOH at 75 C). Rationale: 3.2 wt% > 2.5 wt%, so the gaskets will fail. The bill must include a gasket upgrade or a reduction in caustic. Since the constraint says "gaskets are rated for up to 2.5 wt%", and we cannot modify the deployed part (the system housing), we must either source new gaskets (if permitted as "new catalog parts installed as-sold on the surrounding system" - gaskets are consumables/seals, not the primary device) OR reduce the caustic concentration.
Revised Bill Row 2: Reduce Caustic Concentration: Set caustic to 2.5 wt% NaOH (approx. 0.625 mol/L) at 70 C. Tag: CALCULATED (2.5 g/100g water ≈ 2.45% by volume, 2.5% w/w is standard). Rationale: Stays within the 2.5 wt% limit, preserves gasket integrity, maintains sufficient "bite" if organic interference is managed by the more frequent acid cycle.
4. Verification Test: Conduct a CIP efficacy test (clean-in-place efficiency) after two fortnightly acid cycles. Tag: ASSUMPTION (Standard practice validation). Rationale: Confirms scale removal.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Installability: Low (no hardware change, only schedule and setpoint change).
Operability: Low (operator changes schedule on existing PLC/CIP program).
Maintenance: Neutral (gasket life preserved by staying within rating).
Operational Loss: ZERO (no throughput loss; CIP time may slightly increase due to extra acid cycle, but within standard CIP duty cycles).
Cost: Negligible (chemical cost increase < 5% due to slightly higher caustic use; labor for schedule change negligible).
Parity: SAME burden class, DIFFERENT mechanism (schedule-driven scale control vs concentration-driven organic control).
EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Run 3 cycles of the new schedule (Fortnightly Acid, 2.5 wt% Caustic).
Instruments: Visual inspection of plates after draining; thermocouple mapping of plate surfaces during pasteurization.
Pass/Fail: No blistering observed; temperature uniformity within 1 C across plates; CIP turbidity readings below 1 NTU post-caustic.
Duration: 6 weeks (3 fortnightly cycles).
Kill Criterion: If blistering persists or temperature delta > 2 C, the mechanism is falsified; scale is not the sole driver, or caustic level is insufficient for organics, requiring a different approach (e.g., water softening, which is out of scope for CIP params).

CONSTRAINT BIND
Primary Indicator: Hard-water scale blistering plates (mechanical/thermal damage).
Secondary Indicator: CIP losing bite (chemical efficacy).
The draft violates the constraint by proposing 0.8 mol/L (~3.2 wt%), which exceeds the 2.5 wt% gasket rating. It also misidentifies the primary failure driver (scale) by focusing only on caustic concentration. The revised proposal respects the gasket limit and addresses the scale driver via schedule.

MACHINE REPAIR PASS RESOLUTIONS
1. BILL_UNTAGGED: Resolved. All rows tagged.
2. PHYSICS_DIRECTION_UNSTATED: Resolved. DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT stated explicitly.
3. MECHANISM_CLASS_UNSTATED: Resolved. "MECHANISM CLASS: Chemistry and Schedule Optimization" declared.
4. DEPLOYED-PART CLAUSE: Resolved. No modification to plates or tank. Only changes to CIP schedule and chemical setpoints, and verification/replacement of gaskets (consumables/seals, not the primary device structure) if necessary. Since the constraint states gaskets are rated for 2.5 wt%, and we are staying at 2.5 wt%, no gasket upgrade is required, only verification.
5. PERMITTED-SET CLAUSE: Resolved. Constraint permits raising CIP caustic concentration (within gasket limits) and changing acid descal interval. We are using exactly these axes.
6. EXEMPLAR-REALITY / PREMISE-VALIDITY / CERTIFIED-SYSTEM: Resolved. No new hardware, no custom parts. Only schedule and setpoint changes on existing CIP system.
7. DIRECTION-CORRECTNESS / INPUT-AVAILABILITY / COST-PRICING: Resolved. Direction is correct (reduce scale mass). Inputs are standard CIP logs (turbidity, conductivity) already present. Cost is negligible.
